review.tagline: Python library that runs large LLMs on small GPUs by streaming layers from disk
review.summary: AirLLM splits a Hugging Face model into per-layer shards and keeps only one decoder layer on the GPU at a time, so VRAM need tracks layer size rather than total model size. The README reports Llama 3.x 70B in about 4GB, DeepSeek-V3 671B in about 12GB, and LoRA training of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B under 6GB. Loading goes through a single AutoModel.from_pretrained call, with optional 4bit/8bit compression.
review.audience: Engineers running or fine-tuning very large open LLMs on low-VRAM GPUs
strengths: Runs 70B models in about 4GB VRAM without quantization, distillation or pruning, per the README
One AutoModel.from_pretrained call covers Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Mixtral, Phi, Gemma and others
Includes LoRA training that streams frozen weights layer by layer, with example scripts
Supports Apple silicon via mlx and CPU inference, besides CUDA GPUs
weaknesses: Splitting the model needs large disk space, for example about 360GB for Flash-Next
Speed is bound by disk loading; the README gives no tokens-per-second figures
No HTTP API or server; it is a Python library used with generate()
Newer models need specific transformers versions, and Kimi K3 needs flash-attn on CUDA 12
needs: Needs PyTorch, transformers, bitsandbytes (for 4bit/8bit compression), mlx (macOS), flash-attn and compressed-tensors (Kimi K3)
Models: Llama 2/3/3.1/3.3/4, Qwen 1/2/2.5/3/3.5/3.8, DeepSeek V2/V3/R1, Mistral, Mixtral
